slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI development. Her opposition to the 2025 moratorium was about a ban on state AI laws, not a pause on AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Introduced the AI for ALL Act to create an AI Literacy and Education Commission in the Office of Science and Technology Policy.
Offered a Rules Committee amendment on 21 May 2025 to remove the 10-year ban on state AI laws from H.R. 1; it was rejected 8-4.
Led, with Rep. Doris Matsui, a letter from over 75 members opposing reviving a moratorium on state and local AI laws in the defense authorization bill.
grade_reason: She has spoken about AI (literacy, state regulation, general challenges and public safety) but no statement found acknowledges catastrophic risk, and nothing on AI was found from 2026.
notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. All three statements are from 2025; her press releases for January to November 2026 (pages 0 to 6 of rivas.house.gov press releases) contain nothing on AI. The 1 December 2025 press release with Rep. Matsui has joint quotes (e.g. blocking state safeguards would "leave Americans exposed to escalating risks"), attributed to both members together, so they were left out of statements; they name no catastrophic risk and would be D anyway. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar, September 2026): no source found listing Rivas as a cosponsor, but the congress.gov cosponsor page returned 403 and could not be checked, so this is not confirmed either way. Quotes were read via a page-fetch tool that summarizes pages; wording was returned as quoted text but a reviewer should confirm exact characters.
